cases.visibleGeometry: A cluster of short, angular ridges and raised blocks occupies the northwest quadrant, with an isolated small raised block to its south. A narrow curving line runs just east of the cluster. A separate low rounded rise lies farther south near the line; the remaining ground is subdued.
cases.alternatives: Standing or collapsed modern structures, rock piles, vegetation artifacts, a track and ordinary ground disturbance could account for the shapes.
cases.supportLimits: The angular cluster overlaps a dense patch of interpolated cells, so its sharp shapes cannot be accepted without source-ground inspection. Most surrounding ground is measured.

candidates.nextCheck: Inspect original classified returns and current or historical imagery for buildings, rock piles and interpolation effects.

cases.visibleGeometry: A broad, curving break in slope crosses the patch from the left edge toward the upper-right side. Its upper side is irregular and stippled with small bumps; the lower side is comparatively smooth with scattered low hummocks. A faint straight line crosses the upper-right area.
cases.alternatives: A natural drainage or slope margin, track or field edge and vegetation-related roughness fit the pattern. The isolated hummocks may be ordinary surface variation.
cases.supportLimits: Interpolation follows much of the curving break and several bump clusters. Those details require raw-return confirmation; the smooth lower area is mainly measured.

cases.visibleGeometry: Regular, close-spaced curved ridges occupy the upper-left field; parallel fine ridges also cross the upper-right and lower areas. Straight north-south and east-west linear breaks meet near the centre, separating differently textured ground. A small bright lump lies at the junction.
cases.alternatives: Cultivation rows, field boundaries, a track or drainage line and a small boundary feature explain the pattern.
cases.supportLimits: The boundary lines and central junction include interpolated cells. Most cultivated surfaces are measured, though small scattered gaps remain.

cases.visibleGeometry: Two nearly parallel linear boundaries frame a broad, gently textured strip across the patch. Regular cultivation ridges lie above and below it. A discrete small rounded rise sits near the upper boundary at about x310, y99; a few smaller bumps occur near the lower-right edge.
cases.alternatives: Field margins, track edges or drainage features explain the long lines. The isolated rise could be a tree base, soil or rock pile, or agricultural feature.
cases.supportLimits: Interpolation follows both long boundaries and scattered patches within the strip. The rise is beside an interpolated boundary, so its form needs raw-return verification.

candidates.feature: Small isolated rounded rise beside field boundary
candidates.nextCheck: Inspect original ground returns and imagery to distinguish a persistent mound from a tree base, pile or boundary disturbance.
